input.args: Write a new runbook at docs/runbooks/receipts-stopped.md for the trigger "no receipts sent since last night" / receipts stopped going out. Source material is notes/chat-receipts.md (a chat export where Tomás diagnosed and fixed this twice). Facts to capture: the worker process is a systemd service named larder-worker; jobs queue in the procrastinate_jobs table in the larder postgres database (send_receipt in larder/receipts.py is the procrastinate job that emails the receipt); the deploy script only restarts the web app, not the worker, so a deploy can leave the worker dead (inactive/dead) while jobs pile up as 'todo'; the fix is to check `systemctl status larder-worker`, count todo jobs with `psql larder -c \"select status, count(*) from procrastinate_jobs group by status\"`, start the worker with `sudo systemctl start larder-worker`, and re-run the query to watch todo drain to 0 (about 40/minute last time); failed jobs for bounced/invalid emails are expected and not an incident; if the worker dies again immediately, pull `journalctl -u larder-worker -n 50` and escalate to Tomás (or whoever owns receipts/payments now) in the pantry's ops chat. This is the second time this has happened and the on-call volunteer didn't know what to do, so the runbook needs to let the next volunteer self-serve instead of waiting for Tomás. Also add this runbook to docs/runbooks/README.md's list, consistent with the existing Gateway timeouts entry. Follow the kind's criteria in docs/README.md exactly (lead order, Before you begin/Steps/If it fails sections, one action per step with its expected output). Write the file for real with the Write tool, don't just describe it.

last_message: Added `docs/runbooks/receipts-stopped.md`, listed in `docs/runbooks/README.md`, covering what Tomás worked out in `notes/chat-receipts.md`: check `systemctl status larder-worker`, count queued `procrastinate_jobs`, start the worker, watch `todo` drain (~40/min), treat lingering `failed` bounces as normal, and escalate via `journalctl` + the ops chat if it won't stay up — so the next on-call volunteer can self-serve instead of waiting for Tomás.
